title: Why We Built Mimir Nest
description: A small open-source project built around a simple idea: students shouldn't need ten different places to find the things they need to study, prepare, and build.
author: Sachin Patel
content:
College has a weird way of making simple things complicated.

You need a place to practice DSA. Somewhere else for courses. A spreadsheet for placement preparation. Another website for project ideas. A random document for student perks. And probably a calculator bookmarked somewhere that you've used at least once during the semester.

None of these things are particularly difficult on their own.

The annoying part is that they're scattered everywhere.

That's where Mimir Nest started.

Not as a grand plan to build another "platform for students." Just as an attempt to put useful things in one place.

## What is Mimir Nest?

Mimir Nest is an open-source collection of tools and resources for students.

It brings together things like:

- [CGPA and academic tools](/cgpa)
- [Placement and DSA preparation](/placement-dsa)
- [Project ideas](/projects)
- [Courses and learning resources](/courses)
- [Productivity tools](/pomodoro) (including [Focus Timer](/pomodoro) and [Typing Practice](/typing))
- [Student perks and opportunities](/email-perks)
- [Learning roadmaps](/roadmaps)

Everything is free to use.

And because the project is open source, the idea isn't for a small team to decide what students need and build everything behind closed doors.

Anyone can contribute.

## Why open source?

This is probably the most important part of Mimir Nest.

Students are already building things.

They are making websites, experimenting with AI, learning React, fixing bugs, writing documentation, designing interfaces, and pushing their first repositories to GitHub.

But contributing to a real project can be intimidating.

You don't always know where to start.

Mimir Nest is meant to be one of those places where you can start small.

Fix a bug.

Improve a page.

Add a useful resource.

Improve documentation.

Build a feature.

Or simply open an issue when something doesn't make sense.

The project gets better, and contributors get experience working on something real.

## What we want Mimir Nest to become

We don't have a perfect roadmap for this.

And that's intentional.

The platform will change as people use it and contribute to it.

Some ideas will work.

Some won't.

Some features may eventually be removed entirely.

What matters is that Mimir Nest remains useful rather than becoming another website full of features nobody needs.

The long-term goal is simple:

"Build useful software for students, in the open, with the people who use it."

## Start here

If you're a student, explore the tools and resources.

If you're a developer, look through the repository.

If you find something broken, tell us.

If you have an idea, open an issue.

And if you want to build something, make a pull request.

Mimir Nest is still being built.

That's kind of the point.
